subject: EdgeBio measurement hypotheses and acceptance plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Ramos <lucia@edgebio.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — measurement hypotheses + next steps

Hi Lucia — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff:

Call highlights:
- Primary objective: surface-level batch inference for our variant-calling pipeline and reduce per-sample latency on the interactive review UI.
- Key constraints: average response size ~120 tokens, typical throughput bursts to 30 QPS for short windows, sustained baseline 3–5 QPS.
- Compliance: data stays in your VPC during the Private deployment; no data retention by Redwood beyond logs.

My hypotheses for what will define success in the trial (please flag anything missing):
1) Latency: median tail p95 response <= 250ms for single-sample review requests (95% of trials after warm-up).
2) Throughput: system sustains 25 QPS for 10-minute burst windows with no request failures; graceful degradation beyond that.
3) Cost: estimated cost <= $0.004 per sample (post-quantization and batching suggested by Redwood Optimize).
4) Quality: model-level accuracy metric (EdgeBio's internal variant concordance) no worse than 1.5% delta vs current baseline.

Proposed measurement plan (short):
- Sample workload: Jordan — can you confirm the sample mix and attach a 48-hour representative CSV?
- Readiness: we’ll run a smoke validation (5k requests) and then a load run (100k requests shaped to your burst pattern).
- Acceptance gates: pass p95 latency and <1% 5xx errors; quality measured on a held-out 1k sample set provided by EdgeBio.

Kickoff proposal and owners:
- POC kickoff workshop: Tue 20 May, 10:00 PT (30–45 min) — agenda: network + credential handoff, load generator, metric dashboards. (Owner: Irene)
- Workload handoff & data sample: EdgeBio to share by Mon 19 May (Owner: Lucia)
- Technical runbook & KPI dashboard: Jordan to own instrumentation and alerting; Marissa to coordinate SLO definitions and billing estimates.

Attachments: initial scope + a lightweight KPI template attached for your review.

Next steps: Lucia — can you confirm the 20 May time slot and share the sample workload CSV by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful and mostly aligned. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the UI is sensitive to p95 for interactive reviewers, but we could accept p99 < 400ms for the first iteration if p95 is harder to stabilize.
- Throughput: the 30 QPS burst is accurate; bursts are typically 7–12 minutes long.
- Cost: your number looks promising; can you include GPU type assumptions (g4dn vs a100) in the cost estimate?
- Quality: our concordance metric is measured on your normalized JSON outputs — we’ll provide the metric script.

I confirm we can share a 48-hour sample by Monday EOD; the 20 May slot works — please send a calendar invite.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Ramos <lucia@edgebio.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — measurement hypotheses + next steps

Appreciate the confirmation, Lucia. A few technical details to remove ambiguity and make the acceptance gates testable:

1) Workload shape and tooling
- Please include per-request token distribution (min/median/max) in the CSV. I’ll use Vegeta + a small custom harness to reproduce your burst windows.

2) Latency gating
- We’ll measure cold vs warmed (first 1k requests excluded from steady-state calculations).
- Metric definitions: p50/p95/p99 latency on server-side processing time (exclude network egress) and overall end-to-end. Our dashboard will show both.

3) Throughput and errors
- Acceptance: sustained 25 QPS for a 10-minute window with 99.5% success rate (5xx+timeouts < 0.5%). If you need the more lenient p99 < 400ms option, we can define a secondary gate.

4) Cost assumptions
- Baseline estimates: g4dn.xlarge private hosts (NVIDIA T4) vs a100 80GB dedicated. I’ll attach a short cost sensitivity table after the kickoff once I know batch sizes and quantization target.

5) Quality evaluation
- Please provide the variant concordance script and the holdout set; we’ll run quality checks after the smoke runs and before load runs. Target: delta <= 1.5% to be considered non-regressive.

I attached a minimal sample_workload_spec.csv template (small stub) and a runbook checklist. Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
